utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Madam Registrar, you can call the case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Registrar, and good afternoon to you. Mr. Oric, good afternoon to you. Before we proceed, can you please confirm to us that you are receiving interpretation in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. I am indeed receiving interpretation in my own language and I'm able to follow the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon Your Honours, my name is Jan Wubben lead counsel for the Prosecution and good afternoon to you the Defence as well. I'm here together with co-counsel, Ms. Patricia Sellers, and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben and good afternoon to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. My name is Vasvija Vidovic, together with Mr. John Jones, I represent the Mr. Naser Oric. With us our legal assistant, Miss Adisa Mehic, our legal assistant, and Mr. Geoff Roberts, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic and good afternoon to you and your team. So before we bring in the witness, are there any preliminary matters that you would like to raise? Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Vidovic, I'm just enquiring of you, do you think you could possibly finish this witness by today?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just before our session, I spoke to my colleagues from the Prosecution. If Ms. Sellers is able to stick to what she promised, that she would be finished within ten or fifteen minutes, I will do my best to finish today, because usually I am able to finish with the number of questions I've foreseen with this witness within three hours, or thereabouts. So it should be possible, of course, provided that the witness co-operates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. Let's bring the witness in. Not lose more type. Ms. Sellers do you think you can finish your in-chief in ten or fifteen minutes?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's what I'm aiming for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's perfect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. You are still testifying under oath. I'm just reminding you. We will proceed with the examination-in-chief, then we will have the cross-examination and we are all doing our utmost to try and finish with your testimony today so that you can go home earlier. Let's start, Madam Sellers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Sellers: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you testified about the attack by Muslim forces on Bjelovac on the 14th of December, 1992. You specifically testified that the forces or guards from Bratunac came to Bjelovac after the Muslim forces had retreated. If you know, please tell the Trial Chamber why the Bratunac guards arrived after the Muslim retreat.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were unable to go to Loznica and Zaluzje because that area was blocked, so they went through Serbia and were transported across the river Drina by boat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever come to know who, if anyone, commanded the Muslim forces that attacked Bjelovac on that day?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never learned that, because I don't know who their commander was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea who was in charge of the Muslim forces in the region?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Naser Oric was in charge of Srebrenica. I don't know who was in charge of that action in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the same Naser Oric that you've testified about when we spoke about your employment at the gas station?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know only of one. I don't know any other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Returning just a bit to your days at the gas station, Mr. Petrovic. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber if you knew a person called Kemo?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please give us a physical description of Kemo.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a tall guy, well built. We were on good terms before the war. He would often come to the gas station and filled his car up there at this gas station where I worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Kemo worked prior to the war, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he worked in a company, or if he was self-employed in a private company. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him in a uniform of any kind before the war?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, I did not see him in a uniform. But just before the war started, about 15 to 20 days before that, I saw him wearing the uniform of the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know where he would be a member of the reserve police force? From where would he be a member of the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one occasion, as I was going home, I saw him Turbe, near Potocari, at the checkpoint. He stopped my cousin's car. That was the car of Mladen Petrovic. He was giving me a lift. We knew each other. He saw me in the car and I did not have any problems. He let us through and to go on our way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity, since you've seen him on several occasions and he has spoken to you, did you have an opportunity to learn about his reputation?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean before the war?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, I knew Kemo very well. He was an aggressive man. But regardless of the ethnic background. He would often get into conflict with the police and, so to speak, they couldn't do anything to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it your testimony that Kemo had a propensity toward violence?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it also be your testimony this was well known or this was his reputation prior to the war in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody in Srebrenica knew that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, returning just a bit and here we will try and conclude, returning to your testimony that Naser Oric was in charge of forces in Srebrenica, I would like to ask you, after seeing Mr. Oric at the gas station, did you ever see him in an image, in a print, in a video televised, painted or otherwise, after those days at the gas station?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I worked at the gas station, no. I never saw him in the papers, in any picture anywhere. That was up until the war when he came to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the war, did you ever see him in any papers or print or in any other form?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the war, I saw him in the papers. I don't remember what newspaper that was. I think it was Kravica. A group of soldiers were photographed I think they were standing in front of a cafe, or the youth hall where the village dances were held.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask that the witness be shown 460. It's on Sanctions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, is this the picture that you've just referred to in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you, please, describe for the Trial Chamber where you see Naser Oric on that picture.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he's right here. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour might I ask him to hold --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, could he --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: -- to hold the picture up and point to it so that Your Honours will be able to see. We can put it on the ELMO also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, could you point again, on the photo, so that we can follow you on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Petrovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, the witness points to the individual who appears to be on horseback under the tip of the angle of the roof of the building that stands behind him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour I think it is important to state that it is it a brown horse, at least not a white horse, because there have been references to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Certainly. It shows on the photo. I mean, we only have one photo now, but.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But the transcript refers to white horses all over the place, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But I didn't say white horse, did I?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. I'm just saying it should say it is not a white horse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is a dark horse for all intents and purposes, what we are seeing in the photo now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour I don't know whether you would like him to circle the printed image. It would not -- we might use this photo in the future. I don't know whether you want this witness to make a mark when he's circled or whether it is sufficient --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you can spare this photo and have others like it, at our disposal later on, yes, we can do that. So, Mr. Petrovic, perhaps take that photo back in your hands now and put a big circle around the person -- no. Don't. Don't, because that is the court exhibit. So you need to give him another one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: What we will do is try to provide another clean photo to the registrar, if that were possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: To replace this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This one, it's already marked. So I don't think we can have the witness mark -- put any marks on it. If you have a spare copy of it, then -- but anyway I think the description that I have put on the record suffices.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly. Now, I would ask, could we just have Mr. Petrovic look closely at the photograph and on our Sanction screen we're going to do a slight zoom-in. Mr. Petrovic, do you recognise any other people in this photograph by face or by name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Report to the technicians, please, that Judge Eser's monitor is not functioning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I recognise two of the faces, but I can't remember their names. I saw them quite often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see them quite often before the war, while you were working at the gas station or in some other capacity? Or on some other occasion?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before. Before. While I was still working at the gas station, before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know, of the people that you recognise, were they Bosnian Serbs or Bosnian Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I will just ask that we do a final zoom in and, Mr. Petrovic, I would ask you to look closely and tell me, if you can, what types of weapons are the persons carrying in the picture.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, the first row, the people that are kneeling down, that would be M84 and as far as I'm able to see, because it's quite dark, the ones in the upper row, they have automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Petrovic, after you saw this picture, did you ever see another photo, print, video, or televised image of Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I saw -- I don't know who the witness was, but that was just very briefly. Because in the area where I live, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, we do not really get the Bosnia-Herzegovina channels. We only get Serbian channels, the Belgrade TV, and they do not really broadcast that very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see a televised image of Mr. Oric on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the trial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that the same Naser Oric that you are referring to that you saw when you worked at the gas station?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Ms. Sellers. Madam Vidovic. Cross-examined by Ms. Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mrs. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you are the only Nikola Petrovic born on the 15th of January, 1959 who lived in Bjelovac during the war.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your wife is Rada Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that in your village, the village of Bjelovac -- I have to apologise, Your Honours. I had a small microphone problem. Mr. Petrovic, you told us that in your village of Bjelovac, from spring 1992 until the very attack, there was a lot of tension; that is correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You explained that this tension was the result of the establishment of the parties, the setting up of the night guards?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also explained, in your testimony, that Muslims on one occasion, in March 1992, stopped a bus with a mixed population on board?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They did not stop the bus. That's not what I said. I said that I came to the bus station to the Kriva road, the bus was not there, but I was brought back. They did not let me pass to go to the bus station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your explanation. You also said that you had evacuated your family to Serbia, to Grabovica. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Many other people from Bjelovac and the neighbouring villages did the same.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 90 per cent, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the tensions were growing because of the attacks on the -- by the Muslim forces on some villages in this area?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that there was a growing danger, that there was any danger. I just said that there were some night guards set up. I didn't say that the Muslim forces carried out any attacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like you to have a look at a map.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a segment of a larger map of the military geological institute of the former Yugoslavia, that is the segment entitled "Zvornik." In order to make it easier for the witness and the Trial Chamber to find their way around, we've highlighted the areas that we will be asking this witness about. I would like the map to be placed on the ELMO and the witness to have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, definitely on the ELMO, because otherwise it will be a great strain on anybody's eyes. So let's put it on the ELMO and have the technicians zoom-in, please, the area which is highlighted. Where would you like to start from, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Bjelovac. Your Honour, I have to apologise for having produced such a small map, but this map really includes everything, and includes all the places that are relevant for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am not criticizing you, Ms. Vidovic. I'm just being practical. So just put it on the -- Bjelovac is the three boxes from the bottom right and three boxes from the extreme right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you please take the pointer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, if you take the last four boxes -- square boxes on the right, bottom right, in the top box you will find Bjelovac. So that's where, under -- below Zaluzje and above Loznica.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what we need --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- the technicians to zoom in, so that, yes, okay. But we have still got to overcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's fine now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Petrovic, look at the screen first and you should be able to identify whereby Bjelovac is. Then look at the map on the other side, on the ELMO, and try to show it to us. Yes. For the record, the witness points to Bjelovac. Yes. Next question, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, now would you please point to Sikirici?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please show Sase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Stop for a moment. And for the record, the witness pointed to Sikirici and to Sase on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now would you be so kind and point to Loznica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness points to Loznica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And please show to Biljaca and Zaluzje?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Biljaca and Zalazje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has indicated the villages of Biljaca and Zaluzje on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Voljevica, please. Pobrdje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Voljevica and Pobrdje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please the area of Rakovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And the witness points to the area of Rakovac. 12

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you please, witness, go up the Drina River and show us Suha.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the witness, for the record, has shown the village of Suha, which is just below the other village of Mihaljevici. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mihaljevici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Indeed he also indicates the village of Mihaljevici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lonjin, please.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you please show us Jelav.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And finally the witness pointed to the two villages of Lonjin and Jelav.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If possible, would you please initial this map, not perhaps in all of these spots but just in one single location, just to confirm that you have indeed shown all of these places to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The witness, for the record, has put his initials. That's initials in Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Latin alphabet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that a "N"? The first one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "N," and then the second letter is a "P".

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Petrovic, now, would you please keep the map with you, because we will be referring to it further during the cross-examination. I will now put some questions to you. During your testimony, you said that the tensions grew due to Muslim attacks on some of the villages in that area. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the tension grew due to party elections. Not due to Muslim attacks. Because in the beginning of the war, nobody attacked. Neither Muslims, nor Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, I am now referring to the time from the beginning of the war onwards.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, the beginning of the war. Then, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So it is your testimony that the tension grew due to Muslim attacks on the Serb villages in that area?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you said yesterday about the way that the situation developed in the spring and summer of 1992 is not a complete truth, is it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. It's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It isn't true that the tension in this area grew due to Muslim attacks in the spring and summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the other reason then?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm asking you to answer my questions.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the tension was called [as interpreted] by the Muslim attacks in the area surrounding the village of Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, witness. It is true, isn't it, that in these villages, before the war, these villages that you have just shown to us, therefore that in these villages before the war there was Muslim population. In some villages the Muslims constituted an absolute majority. In some villages they were a relative majority. Whereas in some villages the population was mixed. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of giving evidence yesterday, you stated that before the war, in Bjelovac, there were only four Muslim houses?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Four Muslim households.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that true?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Q.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In showing video footage of an attack on Bjelovac, the Prosecutor showed you a school?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the school is located in the very centre of Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The school is in the area where one leaves Bjelovac, where the exit point is from Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But would you agree that this still constitutes Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am putting to you now that in the vicinity of the school and some 300 metres away from your house, before the war, there used to be 37 Muslim houses. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now read out to you the names of these people, people who were owners of the houses, and please tell me if we come to a single person who did not own a house before the war in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All of these houses are in the immediate vicinity of the school, to the left of the road. Mujic Hajdar.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's across the river. That's in Zaluzje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hasib Mujic?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's in Zaluzje, in the Zaluzje area of Bjelovac. These are what they used to call Muslim Roma inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you just told us that these are Roma from Bjelovac. They were from Bjelovac, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they used to call them Bjelovac Roma inhabitants. However, they lived across the river, in the Serbian part of Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I need to understand a little bit, because this, what is just stated now, the Serbian part of Bjelovac, may be a little bit confusing. I mean, I think I know what he means, but I think he needs to explain. What's the difference between Bjelovac and the Serbian side of Bjelovac? Serbian part of Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Serbian part of Bjelovac has a river flowing through it. The river that comes from Sase, and all the way up to Sikirici was what was called the Serbian part of Bjelovac. Whereas below the river, towards Zaluzje and Voljevica, lived the so-called Bjelovac Roma, or gypsies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, would you agree with me that before the war there was never any kind of a division into the Serbian or Muslim or the gypsy Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war there was no kind of a division or distinction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So this was just a place known as Bjelovac? This is what we are discussing right now.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that true?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, let us not go through the names, because it is rather clear. Please tell us whether the Jahic family is also a Gypsy family. Jahic Ismeta, Jahic Fikret, Jahic Salko, are all of these gypsies?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This was a settlement where no Muslims or Serbs lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But would you agree that these people were still Muslims? These Roma are still Muslims, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I said so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sinanovic, Rahman, Dalibasic Muriz [phoen], are they Roma or not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are Muslims, they lived in the area where the school was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I will not proceed with this any further. These houses that I just mentioned, except for the four houses mentioned by you yesterday, were all burned in May of 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Except for those four houses which were in the area closer to the Serbian part of Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Chamber who burned down these Muslim houses in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These houses in Bjelovac were burned down by some sort of volunteers who had arrived from elsewhere. Some of them were called people from Vukovar and some of them were called just volunteers but I wouldn't be able to tell you anything else about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened with the property owned by Muslim?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was all burned down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you are referring to Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I think that it all burned down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about these volunteers that you have mentioned, they were also Serbs weren't they?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Most likely they were. However, I never checked. I had no such authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Sikirici, more than half of the residents were Muslim Bosniaks, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war, Voljevica was a large village, with over 1300 residents, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these residents were Muslim Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zaluzje had about 620 residents?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but there were a lot of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they Bosnians?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Suha, Mihaljevici and Lonjin, before the war the Muslims constituted majority, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not as familiar with these villages but I think that you are right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mihaljevici was a purely Muslim village; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is right. If you mean Mihaljevici by the Lubostanija bridge [phoen], I think that you are right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, in the course of April and May, 1992, all of these Muslims were brutally forced out of their homes. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present in Bratunac. I was in Bjelovac. However, I heard that this was true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, Mr. Petrovic, I am now referring to the villages that you've just pointed out to us which are located in the vicinity of Bjelovac, not in the vicinity of Bratunac. This place that you're referring to is ten kilometres from Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me about Mihaljevici, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you both about Mihaljevici, Suha, Biljaca.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Biljaca is something else. It is closer to Bjelovac. It's only about a kilometre and a half to two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Voljevica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's four kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zaluzje?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It borders with Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We're doing fine. But it seems that now you've fallen back to the bad habit of not allowing an interval of time between question an answer. You know about it, Madam Vidovic. I'm not going to preach to you. But the witness doesn't. You are both speaking the same language and what is happening is that you are answering her questions immediately, sometimes you won't even let her finish the question. And you are not the only one who is doing this. Madam Vidovic is doing the same. Sometimes she is not even allowing you to finish your answer, and she jumps in with her question. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Please, it's not for my sake. It is for the sake of the ladies and gentlemen behind the glass panes over there, who have got one of the most difficult jobs inside this Tribunal, and that's interpreting live what each one of us is saying into three languages: Into English, into Serbo-Croat, and into French, and they need the cooperation of all of us otherwise they will go home extremely tired and will also not have the best performance from them that we require. So I appeal to you Madam Vidovic and Mr. Petrovic, please be good enough to allow an interval of time between question and answer. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, did I understand you correctly that Zaluzje borders with Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Voljevica is about three kilometres away from Bjelovac? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Biljaca?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Biljaca is about a kilometre or a kilometre and a half away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic, do you know that many of the Muslims who had been expelled, maltreated in those villages, many of them had been killed?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any of it. I didn't take part in it, and I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber how far Sase are from Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those people who were expelled, in the course of April and May, 1992, they were captured, detained in the Sase camp. Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was about three kilometres away from where you were. You did not hear about the fact that dozens of people had been killed there, including women and 11 small children. This is not something that just happens every day. People talked about it, did they?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was not in Sase. I was in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, that does not answer the question. It's being put to you that people would still talk about these things, the Sase detention centre where these people were being imprisoned and killed, even though it was in Bjelovac that these people would be talking about, the Sase place. The question basically boils down to the following: Irrespective of the fact that you lived in Bjelovac and not in Sase, did you hear about this Sase detention place, correction centre or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were stories and rumours that Muslims had been expelled, but I don't know about the camp in Sase. I know that in Bratunac they were gathered there, but I didn't hear anything about Sase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic, not only should you know about those events, but, in fact, I put it to you, you were an active participant in those events.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 13th of May, 1992, you were in a unit of Slavojub Rankic that attacked the Muslim villages of Voljevica and Zaluzje, burned those two villages down, and killed dozens of civilians, including women and children. People saw you there. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true that I took part in the cleansing of Voljevica and Zaluzje. As far as I know nobody ever mentioned my name or saw me there. I would like to see the evidence and who was it that mentioned Nikola Petrovic as a participant of the cleansing of Voljevica and Zaluzje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you claim that you did not -- that you were not in Zaluzje and Voljevica on the 13th of May, 1992; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not there, that's right 100 per cent true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was another part of your question. Because this is why I wouldn't like you to put several questions into once. The first part of your question, was suggesting that he formed part of a specific unit. And perhaps you can put that question again, whether, on the 13th of May or thereabouts, he formed part of a -- you tell him which unit, please, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. This is precisely what I wanted to ask. In May and not only in May, in fact, but throughout the better part of 1992 but, in particular, in May, you were a member of Slavojub Rankic's unit, am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Petrovic, thousands of people who were expelled from these villages that I mentioned roamed the woods around the villages in the spring, summer and autumn of 1992. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The villages from Voljevica and Zaluzje, Abdulici, Tegari, tried to go back to their homes. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps they did try to do that during the night, but I don't know whether they tried to do that during the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is true that they left their fields sown with crops?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is true, is it not, that these people were under constant attack, that ambushes were set up for them by the Serbian troops. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, where? Where were the guards? Where were they attacked? You did not specify the locations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will come to that later, but let me now ask you quite specifically, on the roads leading to Voljevica, Zaluzje, Abdulici, Tegari; do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said that they had been expelled. They did not live there if they were expelled. Though went down to Srebrenica, towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like you to ask the witness not to comment on my questions. I am talking about ambushes, and I am claiming, I put it to you that ambushes were set up for Muslims on the routes they used as they tried to go back to their villages of Voljevica, Zaluzje, Abdulici, and Tegari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in this area a large number of mines were laid on all possible routes, including the streambeds used by Muslims to move about. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that mines were laid a bit further up from the Serbian village of Bjelovac, in front of the line that we held. Now, as for the other villages, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that many Muslims on those routes that I just mentioned, leading to Voljevica, Zaluzje, Abdulici, and Tegari were captured and taken to Serb prisons throughout 1992?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that, in fact, this caused tensions in the area where you lived, not only the attacks that you mentioned yesterday in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I could agree with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you spoke about the attacks on Loznica, in the summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, right from the beginning of the war, Loznica was a Serbian stronghold, the stronghold of the Serbian forces and this was the area where ambushes were set for Muslim civilians who were trying to reach Abdulici and Tegari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that, but they didn't have to go to Tegari via Loznica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this is where sniper and machine-gun nests were positioned, where hundreds of Muslims were killed as they tried to get to their property during the night. Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is impossible that that many of them could be killed during the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about the attack on Zalazje and Azlica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, the headquarters of an entire battalion of the Serbian army was located in Zalazje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many of them there were, but there were Serbian troops in Zalazje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that heavy artillery was stationed there and that fire was opened from that heavy artillery daily on the surrounding Muslim areas, in particular, Potocari and Srebrenica. Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not at Zalazje, but it is possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is possible that heavy artillery was positioned there and that it was used to shell those areas?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified in detail yesterday about the attack of the Muslim forces on Obadi. On the 12th of June, 1992. Would you agree with me that Likari is in the immediate vicinity of Obadi? I would like to ask you now to have another look at the map that we've used. I hope that you have it here. Yesterday you showed Obadi here to the Trial Chamber. I think Obadi are quite visible here on this map. Could you now please show the area of Likari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has indicated the town of -- or the village of Obadi and the one -- and of Likari on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that Likari are less than one kilometre away from Obadi? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is true, is it not, that the Pous hill is right above your father's house, about three hundred metres away from it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is the hill from the house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two kilometres away from where my house and our houses were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your clarification. Judging by what you said here in your testimony yesterday, your brother told you, in great detail, about what happened in that area.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me about the fall of Obadi, but if you ask me more questions, I will answer you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You must know that Likari is the first Muslim village that was attacked, burnt down, and whose population was expelled from the village in this entire region and they were attacked precisely by the unit from the Obadi area. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Obadi is a small village. Please, tell the Trial Chamber how many houses were there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe about 20 households.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So everybody knew what was happening. Did your brother tell you that five Muslim women were captured in Likari on the 24th of April, 1992 and taken to Obadi where they were raped, until the 12th of June, 1992 continually until they were found by Muslims and set free. Did your brother tell you about that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He never mentioned that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Things like that do not happen every day, do they?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. If I knew about it, I would tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I will be asking you some questions that pertain to the attack itself. As you testified yesterday, you said that you were awoken by shots, which means that the fighting in Bjelovac started early?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that you gave a statement to the investigators of the -- this Tribunal, in May, year 2000?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was in Milici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You signed that statement, did you not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, on that occasion, that you went to your sister's house and that there you found your brother, Milan Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mladen Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mladen Petrovic. His nickname was Mile?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is my cousin, in fact my nephew, my brother's son. He also lives in Mileci [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification. In fact, you went to Petko Vucetic's house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Petko Vucetic, Mladen Petrovic, and you were, at that time, fighters of the Bratunac Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the Bjelovac Brigade. In fact it did belong to -- it was under the Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your sister's house, you spent the entire day there, yes?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, together with your brother and your brother-in-law, you participated in the fighting. You opened fire on the attackers from the house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you -- do you want to tell us that you just sat there quietly, waiting for the attackers to pick you up?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on guard duty in the first shift. The weapons was left behind in the trenches for the next shift to pick up. So I did not have weapons with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you want to say that your brother and your brother-in-law did not have any weapons either?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brother that was in the house had never used any weapons ever, because he was retarded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about your brother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother-in-law did not have any weapons with him. The weapon remained in the trench in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that many people had weapons except, at that point of time, you, and what you said. And would you agree that many people had weapons in their houses and fired at the attackers?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your house was set on fire after it became dark on the 14th of December, 1992. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not after it became dark. It was rather early in the morning, before sunrise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I just told you that you gave a statement in 2000, and now I would like to draw your attention to a part of your statement given to the investigators so that we may clarify it. On page 2, paragraph 4, if needed I can give you this text, you said the following, and I am quoting. "After I moved to my sister's and when the dark fell, when the light fell, I saw from my sister's house that three soldiers in uniform and two persons in civil clothes, entering my house." Then further down you said: "There were about -- in the house there -- they stayed for about five to ten minutes. And the moment they came out I saw flames coming out of one of the rooms facing the main road of the village. The house was not fully gutted by the fire. At this time, there was an intense exchange of fire." Therefore, witness, would you like me to give you the statement so that you can take a look at it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said explicitly to the investigators that you saw your house being set on fire after it became dark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, one moment, because you asked the witness -- you said, therefore, witness, would you like me to give you the statement so that you can take a look at it. And on my transcript here I have "no audible response," which I confirm. I did not hear the witness say yes or no, because, Ms. Vidovic, you had already jumped in with your next question. So let's go back to that. Do you want to have the statement available in front of you, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no need for that. I know the statement almost by heart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So your next question, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me. Might I make a suggestion. In terms of clarification, I think Madam Vidovic is talking about it being dark. The statement says when light fell. If we can just get clarification as to what does the witness understand by that phrase, I think we might be able to move forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, the witness did not use that phrase in English. That's a translation of what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So perhaps we can leave him -- let him explain to us according to him when these events, what time of the day these events took place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That happened in the morning, very early in the morning. Perhaps the term used was "when the dark lifted." You know maybe that's what they were trying to say, "when the dark lifted," rather than when the light fell, because it was in the morning. I don't know if this makes it clearer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This kind of a phrase, in our language, does not really exist, the phrase "when the darkness lifted" or vanished, doesn't it? What would that mean when the dark vanished?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would mean that it became light, that the day broke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Which expression would you have used, if you remember? Which expression would you have used or did you use with the persons who were interviewing you, in your own language, to explain what time of the day this particular event happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This event took place early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue, Ms. Vidovic, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the statement given to the investigators of this Tribunal, you said, and I just pointed it out to you, that at that time there was a very intense exchange of fire. You said, actually, that your house had been set on fire at a time when there was a very intense exchange of fire. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember stating it in those terms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now read out to you the following passage on page 2, the penultimate passage in the B/C/S version, which is approximately the same in the English version. You said: At this time there was an intense exchange of fire. I saw that after my house many other houses in Bjelovac were also set on fire. Did you state this, witness?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember saying this about the exchange of fire. However, I remember very well stating this about the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, witness. How far is Sikirici from the location where you were at the time when you said that you saw the houses burning in Sikirici?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 300 to 400 metres. Sikirici borders with Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally did not see what was going on in Sikirici?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was able to see only the fire rising from the houses. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, during your testimony, you said that towards the end of the day some kind of a reinforcement arrived from Bratunac. You said that these were the guards and then the Muslim forces withdrew. Then you explained that this took place at around 3.30. Therefore, it is true, isn't it, that the Muslim forces --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Pardon me. I hate to interrupt. I believe that the witness's testimony was that the Muslim forces retreated and then the guards or forces from Bratunac came, which is slightly different from the question that is being put to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. I will reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's actually in the inverse unless it has been interpreted the opposite way to us, because here, what we have in the transcript is that you said that these were -- these were the guards and then the Muslim forces withdrew. And yesterday you definitely hinted or agreed that, first the Muslims, forces withdrew and after that, the guards came in.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Witness, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you could re-ask it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will, I will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, during your testimony, you said that the Muslim forces withdrew and then only afterwards did the guards arrive from Bratunac; that's what you said?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually, what is true is that the Muslim forces withdrew due to a very intense counterattack of the Serb forces. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is true, isn't it, that most of the houses were set on fire after the counterattack from Bratunac was launched.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That isn't true either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described the defence lines of the village. You said that the defence lines of the village were located on the slope below the Bjelovac forest, and stretched out to the most distant houses in Sikirici. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So the defence lines of the Sikirici village stretched immediately along the houses in Sikirici. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that the Muslims withdrew on the 14th of December, 1992, at around 3.00 or 3.30. Then you said that the Serbs had Bjelovac under their control for another two days. I'm asking you this now, it's true, isn't it, that the Army of Republika Srpska evacuated people from Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You yourself also left Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 15th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not see what was going on in Bjelovac after that time because you weren't there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was across from Bjelovac, in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were unable to see who was in Bjelovac then -- actually, was it Muslim civilians or Muslim troops, you were unable to see that. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore you are confirming to me now that you were unable to see that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was unable to see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You also were unable to see the animals being led away.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's -- once this has been raised, let's clear this up. In other words, what is being asked, what you are confirming is that you were not able to see animals being taken, being led away? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have just one more question an then we could break, if the time is convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, the counterattack which was launched with the arrival of the Serb forces from Bratunac, represented, actually, the intense fighting which took place from the 14th of December, 1992, until the Serbs took control of Bjelovac again. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no counter attack whatsoever, because the forces were pulled out of Bjelovac on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will return to that later. I think that I've just completed with one topic of my examination, and this would be a convenient time for a break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we will have a break of 25 minutes, starting from now. Thank you. Please try, everybody, try to be punctual so that we do not lose any time, if possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's continue. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you, Your Honours. I couldn't deal without the presence of our assistant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, we will now return to the wider area of Bjelovac in the spring of 1992. During your testimony yesterday, you said, in regards of the weapons possessed by the Serb forces in your area, that originally it belonged to the civilian protection. The civilian protection in our area, however, never had any weapons, is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. However, I meant the reserve forces. Perhaps I didn't use the right expression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually, these were the weapons of the Territorial Defence, the ones that had been confiscated from the Muslims. Did you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did understand it; however, I don't know whether it was confiscated from the Muslims. I don't know. I think these weapons came from the Bratunac, from the command. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The JNA and SDS distributed weapons to the villagers in your area, large amounts of various types of weapons. This was done before the war and continued in the beginning of the war. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the JNA and what you mean; however, the weapons were distributed. Now as to whether this was done by the SDS party, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It is not true that the weapons were given -- or issued only to hose who were on duty while they were on duty, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is not true that the weapons were issued only to those persons who were on duty and while they were on duty.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapons were kept only in trenches by those persons who were on duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, I would like to ask the usher to show Exhibit D101 to the witness. This is a document of the Bratunac Brigade, number 01320211, which shows salaries paid out for the May of 1992, which is an excerpt from the set that I described earlier. Witness, now please take a look at the page with the number 01320211. And please take a look at the entry for Rakovac and there follows a description, the first platoon, Rakovac is the place that you showed to us on the map and you told us how far it was from Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is five to six kilometres away from Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, please take a look at this document. It has an entry -- or rather, it has a column, first and last name, year of birth, weapons, and then employment address. I would like to ask you to take a look at this table, take a look at number 2, where it says Petrovic, Janko, born in 1962, PM-72. The same information can be found next to number 15, Milovanovic Stojadin [phoen], and then take a look at number 20, Miladin, Stevic [phoen], both of these persons were issued PM-72. PM-72 is a machine-gun, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And AP stands for automatic rifle, is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that this list shows that the persons listed here were issued with weapons as early as May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This list does not pertain to Bjelovac. This pertains to the Bratunac Brigade, Mrs. Vasida [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness I'm asking you about Rakovac now. We're dealing with Rakovac now. Do you agree --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about Rakovac. I don't even know these people. These are not the people from our company. These are people from Rakovac Company and Rakovac is towards Zaluzje and Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. However, Mr. Petrovic, based on this list, it seems that a lot of these people were issued with machine-guns?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, looking at this list, I would say yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. This is it for this exhibit. Now please, I would like you to show the witness Exhibit D103. D103, please. Once again this is the document of the Bratunac Brigade, listing salaries for May of 1992. There is a list of soldiers who had 102-millimetre mortars. Please take a look at this list, witness. Yesterday, in the course of your testimony, you mentioned Pobrdje several times. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned Pobrdje only when I said that my father went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And you also said that your sister lived there. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not my sister, but my father's sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Your father's sister. Therefore you had relatives in that place, is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My aunt lived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, witness. Now please take a look at this list. The first five persons are from Pobrdje. Do you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know some of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us, who do you know?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Savo Lukic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The title says "list of soldiers of platoon with 120-millimetre mortars". So it is true that they had these 120-millimetre mortars, is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on this list, it would seem so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Savo Lukic was servicing a mortar?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because he said "no" before you had finished the question, or rather halfway through. So, could you please repeat the question and then he will tell us what he was saying "no" for. Because, as it is, it seemed to be, he stopped you when he said -- do you know that Savo Lukic, and he said "no" then you continued with the rest of the question, which he never answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you knew Savo Lukic, right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that you did not know whether or not he was assigned to the mortar -- to service the mortar.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you something else, in relation to this. A 120-millimetre mortar is a heavy artillery piece which is highly Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. destructive. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that, but I never used it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if there were any mortars in this area of Pobrdje, around Bjelovac, within an area of five square kilometres, at least as off May 1992 and onwards?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber the location, where these artillery pieces that you know about, were deployed.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that. I don't know where they were deployed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there were such weapons there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. Based on this list, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic, you spoke yesterday about mobilisation. This happened from mid-April 1992 onwards. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony, you said that you yourself had been mobilised on the 18th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that the other residents of Bjelovac and the surrounding villages had also been mobilised and you were no exception in this regard. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not an exception.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask the usher to show a document to the witness. This is an excerpt from a book, a registry of military personnel, VOP8A. It is a large book, and the excerpt runs from page 01315496 to 1 -- 01315585, and this is the list of the personnel of the 2nd Infantry Battalion. Could you please look at the list 01315571 and then the page after that, in order to clarify things for the Trial Chamber, and let me explain to you that page 01315572 is, in fact, the second part of the page 01315571, because, apparently not all columns could have been scanned on the same page. So these two pages should in fact be looked at in -- as a single page. Could you please have a look at this number, 85. Under number 85, that would be your name, Nikola Petrovic, father's name, Mirko. Year of birth, 1959?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at the next page. It says here that you were mobilised on the 18th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the next page, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at the first column. It says here date of entry into the armed forces, then you have the date here. And it is empty for those persons where the same date would apply.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that. It says 18th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now please look at number 82, that's Slavoljub Rankic, father's name, Nedjo, year of birth 1951. That is the commander of your company. Is that so, that's the person I asked you about?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that this document provides accurate information?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like this document to be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This document -- however you have not given --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. You haven't yet given a number to the previous document. So would he need to start with that one, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. REGISTRAR: D252.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That will be Defence Exhibit D252. And this document will be D253.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, the 18th of April, 1992, is the time when the Muslims in Bratunac and Srebrenica area received the order to surrender their weapons. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, as you testified, you told us that you had been issued a weapon only for defensive purposes.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you claiming now that it is true that you received a weapon just for the purpose of defending your villages?
