utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the 18th of April, 1992, as of that date, you were a member of the Territorial Defence in Bratunac or its section which was the Bjelovac TO. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was not a village guard. This was a regular unit of the Serbian Territorial Defence. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were civilian guards. No Territorial Defence. We only defended Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is your testimony. In Sase there was a Territorial Defence unit, just as it did in Rakovac, Pobrdje, am I correct? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably there were such units. I didn't go there, but probably there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An officer from Bratunac would come to Bjelovac and organise the units, the unit. You told us that he would come and leave, that he would visit the mobilised people and assign persons to each checkpoint and sentry points. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were checkpoints and sentry points in Bjelovac and the area around it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This officer, therefore, visited, monitored and assigned people who had been mobilised in Bjelovac. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence in Bjelovac was a well-organised unit, is it not so?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From at least May, 1992, and onwards, you received your salaries from Bratunac, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours excuse me I think I should have jumped up a bit earlier I just want to say there was a bit mischaracterisation of the testimony. I think we had a question as to whether there was a Territorial Defence in Bjelovac and the answer from the witness was "no," and then a subsequent question that said: "The Territorial Defence of Bjelovac was a well organised unit." The witness did say "yes," but, I mean, after the witness having said no about a Territorial Defence, to place that phrase in the question is a slight mischaracterisation of the witness's prior testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct. When that goes on the record, it doesn't really change anything. Most of what is being said is hypothetical. Basically it's ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was hoping I would not be forced to use this other document, but I'll -- now I would like the usher to show the witness document, which is a list -- document 012320441, the Territorial Defence in Bjelovac, a list of mobilised persons by platoon. The document is also referring to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is an excerpt from the whole document, which runs from page 01820384 to 01320458, salaries for July 1992. Witness, could you please look at the first page of this document. Could you please look at what it says at the top of this document. Do you agree that it says the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Hercegovina, municipality of Bratunac, Bjelovac TO, which means the Territorial Defence of Bjelovac. Could you please look at this list.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where it says, under number 7, Petrovic, father's name Mirko, Nikola, is that your name?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, does this now change your opinion as regards the existence of this unit? In other words, doesn't this document show that you were a member of the Territorial Defence in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document, I suppose is being tendered, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it is being received as Defence Exhibit D254.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Now I would like to ask the usher to put defence Exhibit D91 on the ELMO. This is the list of people from the military post code containing names of the persons who received compensation of travel costs for 1992. This is again an excerpt from a long document. I will now dictate the number for the record. That's 01319723 to 01319866.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask you to look at page which has this computer generated number 01319818 entitled, the Bjelovac Company. Could you please look at this list. In fact, did you find this, Witness? Where it says the Bjelovac Company?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Bjelovac Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at the name under number 588, Ilic S Novo. Do you know Mr. Novo Ilic?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please now look at the name under number 600, Milos Jovanovic, and 603, Milenko Jovanovic. Are these people that you said that their houses were burnt in the village of Jovanovici in 1992, on the 14th of December?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were also members of the Bjelovac Company in October, 1992, were they not? And from then onwards?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Milos Jovanovic was an old man, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now could you look at the next page. Your name is under number 654, Petrovic M Nikola. Number 654, that would be you, right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. You can remove this document, and I would now like to -- you to show another Defence Exhibit to the witness, that would be Defence Exhibit D88. This is the list of persons in military post codes, 2465/5. Persons who received their salaries in October 1992. That is also an excerpt from an entire document. Witness, you do not have to look at the entire document so as to save some time, Could you please look at the next page, 01319811, it says, "Armoured and Mechanised Unit." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now look at number 233 and 234, that would be Matic Gordana, and Matic Snjezana, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these people from Bjelovac, daughters of Mrs. Slavka Matic?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my question in this regard is: In Bjelovac itself, an Armoured and Mechanised Unit was deployed in Bjelovac, do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Radivoje Radovic, nicknamed Raso, was commanding the unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that man?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that he was not from -- he was not a local.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he was in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, as you testified yesterday, you told us that, apart from some light weapons for maybe 30 to 40 people, in other words rifles, you had not received any other weapons, equipment or other things, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereas, in fact, you in Bjelovac had armoured personnel carriers, tanks, at least as of September 1992. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not -- I'm not sure about the exact date, but, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like the usher to show the witness document that bears the number 02158988, it is a report on the crime trends in September, 1994. In fact, it is a report that was written by the military Prosecutor, Captain Todor Todorovic. Witness, could you please have a look at that document. You will agree with me that this presents a series of events that the Prosecutor dealt with in that time period. For us, the relevant page is 02158997. It appears under number 3 that it says Milorad Pajic. Did you find it witness? That is on page bearing the computer generated number 02158997. Did you find that page?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the lower part of the text there is number 3 and then it says Milorad Pajic, member of the Armoured and Mechanised Company in Bjelovac, allegedly professional soldier with the contract from the military post code 884 in Banja Luka, because there are grounds for suspicion that on the 14th of September, 1992, at around 10.30 p.m. in the village of Bjelovac, near Bratunac, he threatened a member of the Bjelovac Company, Nikola Petrovic, that he would kill him and put a pistol to his forehead. After Nikola Petrovic managed to disarm him, he went to a nearby tank, fired it up, and put a shell into the breech and threatened that he would fire a shell on to the house of the same soldier. Nikola Petrovic, that would be you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this report by the military Prosecutor indicates that, in September, 1992, there was an Armoured and Mechanised Company stationed in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: More over, in that company, in addition to people from Bjelovac, there were also soldiers under contract who had arrived there from various cities. This Pajic person arrived from Banja Luka, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. None of these people were locals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Why is it that yesterday, when you spoke about the weapons in Bjelovac, you never mentioned about there being tanks and APCs?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like for this document to be tendered into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So it is document, which is being tendered by the Defence, is being marked D255.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Territorial Defence of Bjelovac, just like other units in that area, starting in November of 1992 and onwards, were part of the Bratunac Brigade. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They became part of its battalions, is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I will now show you a document, Defence Exhibit D92. This is a list of military conscripts of the 4th Battalion and pertains to their salaries for December of 1992. Would you please take a look at this document. Mr. Petrovic, this document has several pages. Please go through the document. It says on top the "4th Battalion," and then it goes on to list the names, and I will ask you about certain names. First you have the 1st Company, its units. Then you have mortars. Then there is the 2nd and the 3rd Company. Now please take a look at the 4th Company, which can be found on page 8. Page 8, the 4th Company. So this battalion had four companies; am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It seems that your name is on the list for the 4th Company. Please take a look at the name under 264, where it says Nikola Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 263 is Milan Petrovic, son of Mirko. Is that your brother?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 266 is Petko Vucetic. This is your sister's husband; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And the first person on this list is Slavoljub Rankic, who is the commander of the 4th battalion and I already asked you about him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, witness. Now please take a look at page 1 of the document. Under page 1, or rather on page 1, under the title, it says: Sreten Petrovic, son of Ilija, of the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that in December of 1992 he was the commander of this battalion?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The headquarters was in Sase?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the first page, Mr. Petrovic, there are a number of names under the title, the 1st Company. Now, please turn to page 2 which has the computer number 01320784. And then look at the sub-title, the fourth squad, which is somewhere in the middle of the page, under number 54. We see Kosta Rankic, son of Sreten, commander of the third squad, second platoon and then a number of names follow from number 55 to number 64. Please take a look at these names. I am reading the names. Milojko; Andric, Danica; Sretanic; Milovanovic, Kristina; Rankic, Nada. These are all females names; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is true, isn't it, that the military conscripts of the 4th Battalion in December of 1992, included some of the women from Sase and Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were cooks there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look at the name under 62, Stanko -- Vojka Milovanovic, daughter of Stanko. Do you know Mrs. Milovanovic? She used to live in Sase at the time.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that she is from Sase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look at page 3 of this document. The long computer number is 01320785. It says, underneath, "the mortar platoon," and then we see that this platoon had three squads. Please look at these names. Do you know any of these people?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this Milovanovic person is from Sase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to that, I will ask you this. You lived in this area. You are very familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm very familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you once again. Do you know where these mortar platoons were deployed?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this was in Sase, I truly don't know because I didn't go there. Otherwise, I would tell you. And I think that this pertains to Sase, judging on this name, Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know any of the other people on the list?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you witness, please proceed. Please take a look at the following page. The computer-generated number is 01320786. Please look at the bottom of that page, where it says "the second squad." All the way down at the bottom, where it says "the second squad." Please take a look at the notation which is next to number 143, Milan Milo Milinkovic, 19th of December, 1992. Deserted. Then it says Ratko Relic, 20th of December, 1992, deserted. Then number 145, Miodrag Grujicic, deserted on the 20th of December, 1992. Mr. Petrovic, do you agree with me that the Bratunac Brigade, judging by this document, had very accurate records of the presence of their troops and any desertions; am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now please take a look at page 8 once again. This is the page where you saw previously a list for the 4th Company. And then please take a look at the text that follows the signature of the commander of the 4th Battalion, Sreten Petrovic. It reads the other persons from the 4th Company were killed, were wounded or deserted. It's true, isn't it, that the command of the 4th Battalion had very accurate records of those who participated in combat activities?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 4th Company was active in the very centre of Bjelovac, isn't that right, that's your company? I'm speaking about your 4th Company.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what period of time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm now referring to December of 1992.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It's true, isn't it, that these persons listed here were killed or wounded in the attack in December as they were fighting Muslims. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this document has already been admitted into evidence and has exhibit number. Now I would like to ask the usher to show the witness another document from the Bratunac Brigade, which has number 1 -- 01320813. This is a document which comes from the set 013781 and goes to the number 01320876, the entire document has 96 pages and I would like to ask the witness to look at the first page which has the following ERN number, 01320813.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will see that it says here the list of soldiers of the 2nd Infantry Battalion, and this is the salary list for December of 1992. Please take a look at the page which has the number 01320813. You will see that there are names of soldiers, their duties, and then column 3 is days spent. Underneath you will see the name Mila Bozic, commander of the battalion. Now please turn to the last page of this document that I just gave you, it has the Prosecutor's number 01320830. This is this long computer-generated number. Please take a look at this page and then turn to the bottom of that page, where it says "recapitulation, salaries for soldiers of the 2nd Infantry Battalion for the December of 1992." Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Underneath it says: Commander of the battalion, nine -- rather command of the battalion, 9 soldiers. The 1st Company, 108 soldiers. The 2nd Company, in Pobrdje, 112 soldiers. The 3rd Company, called Drinska, 218 soldiers. The platoon of mortars, 55 soldiers. And I think there is the term "scouts" here. I think that pertains to these soldiers. And underneath it says, "a total of 502 soldiers for the 2nd Infantry Battalion." Mr. Petrovic, all of the places listed here are the ones that you showed us on the map today earlier. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let us go back to the first page of that document, where it says "lists". And look under the number, command of the battalion -- or rather look under the entry, command of the battalion where you see the commander of the battalion and, after that, there are 108 names. I will not dwell on this for very long, but please take a look at the page 013201 -- 0817. Please take a look at that page and the first four names listed there. Under number 100, we see Pero Ivanovic. Where it says "soldier" and then in parenthesis, "Kunjerac." Then 101 is Mita Loncarovic [phoen] also from Kunjerac. 102 is Lazar Miluninovic [phoen], the same place, and 103, is Nebeko Nitic [phoen], again from the same place. Let me ask you something about Kunjerac. You mentioned Kunjerac yesterday and you said that, that it was near Bjelovac. Please tell the Chamber what exactly is Kunjerac and how far is it from Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kunjerac is a hill just outside of Bjelovac and it is linked to Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, witness. Kunjerac is an area where the water works were, which was a real military stronghold with a large number of soldiers, am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kunjerac was important for the entire defence line of Bjelovac, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. There was the water plant there, supplying Bjelovac with water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Supplying Bratunac with water interpreter:

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Jelav Company was deployed there.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. They came from Bratunac, but I don't know what company they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now please take a look the at Page 5 of the document where it says, Somewhere under number 108, it says the 1st Company, Jelav, a total of 108 soldiers. Then underneath there, there is the name Nebusa Lukic - commander of the 2nd Company. And then there is a list of 112 names. Please go all the way down to name 112 where you will find the following words, the 2nd Company, Pobrdje, a total of 112 soldiers. Pobrdje is the place that you have shown us on the map.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's the first village after Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now please take a look under the text where it reads, the 2nd Company, Pobrdje. There is a name Milan Lazic, commander of the 3rd Company called Drinska. Have you found that? This is on page with the ERN number 01320821. Have you found this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at the name Milo Lazic where it says commander of the 3rd Drinska Company. Witness, please tell the Trial Chamber where was the headquarters of the Drinska Company, the Drina Company, if you know? Could you look at the list, do you know any of the people?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please let me have a moment to look at it. I think that this was probably somewhere in the area of Bratunac, most of the names here are unknown to me. Practically all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at the name under number 210, 210. It says Pero Jovanovic, wounded. Do you know Mr. Jovanovic, Pero?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was not a person that you mentioned, whose house had been burned down?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is an elderly man from Jovanovici that I mentioned, his name was Petar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please now look at page 16. It says here "total for the Drinska Company, 218." And then below that it says, "the Scouts Battalion," or "Reconnaissance Battalion." Do you find that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Reconnaissance Battalion [platoon], Crveni Perica, and underneath that Bosko Neskovic, platoon commander." I want to ask you something about that. Bosko Neskovic was a very well known person in this area. Did you hear about him?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the platoon commander, was he not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, reconnaissance platoon, Crveni Perica, the word "Crveni," read in English refers to the red berets, does it not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I would like you to have a look at the name under number 14 on this list. It says Rada Jovanovic. Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now go to the next page, that's page 17. Could you now please look at numbers 44, 45, and 46. In fact, 44, 45 and 46. Did you find that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next to the number 44 you have the name Slobodan Despotovic, [volunteer], [killed]. Then Radoslav Djukic [volunteer], [killed]. Then Miodrag Cvijic [volunteer], [killed]. My question in this regard is: Mr. Petrovic, it's true, is it not that in the Bjelovac area a large number of volunteers from Serbia and the Serbian Krajina in Croatia fought?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Bjelovac. That would be in the Bratunac Brigade. My answer to that would be "yes," to Bratunac. There were -- there weren't many of the volunteers in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I'm asking this question, I'm referring to the Bjelovac area and that includes the villages in an area of several kilometres, Zaluzje, Voljevica, Biljaca; am I correct when I say that there were many volunteers fighting there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I understand the rapidness of which the witness is responding to Madam Vidovic's question. I just was wondering, could she couch it in a time period. She's couching a broad area, and that's already caused a bit of confusion. Could we just be a bit specific about what time period your question pertains to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Quite a valid remark. Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour, but I believe that it is quite clear, because I showed the -- to the witness, he sees that and I said loud and clear that these are the payrolls for December 1992 and we're talking about people who were in those units in December 1992. I don't know how much more specific I could be. I think that the witness understood me quite clearly. Thank you very much, witness. Let us go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So -- one moment. Your answer is an oblique one. Your last question to the witness was "am I correct when I say that there were will volunteers fighting there, that is in Bjelovac, Zaluzje, Voljavica, et cetera. So your question is, because the witness answered "yes" so we take it, for the record that what your question referred only to December and that the witness is answering only in relation to December 1992. Because I don't think that the question, when you put that question, you were limiting it to December, Ms. Vidovic. And I don't think that the witness was understanding you to be limiting it to December 1992. That was a question that arose out of this series of questions, but I don't think we understood it to be limited by the time frame of this particular document. That's how I understood it at least. Please correct me if I am wrong. I mean, you are free to ask any question. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour. In this series of questions, my questions were limited to the documents, but I will take up on your suggestion and the suggestion of my learned colleague from the Prosecution and we will try to define every question in precise temporal terms. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I will go back to what we were discussing now. All those units then were present in this area in December 1992, the units that I mentioned, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all those units took part in the fighting between the 14th and the 17th of December, 1992, is it true?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to the entire area where the fighting was going on, in that time, including what I just mentioned, Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I showed you a little while ago a name, Slobodan Despotovic, a volunteer who was killed. He's on page -- one of the pages of this document. Did you hear about Mr. Despotic [as interpreted] by any chance?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. I will now like a video clip to be played to the witness, that is the Defence Exhibit D97, but I would like the witness to retain this document, because I will be asking some other questions related to this document, so I would like the usher to leave this document with the witness. Thank you. Because we will be needing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, Judge Eser has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just a question of clarification. When you take page 17, which we have in front of us, the last line, it would say 31 days spent. We are talking about December 1992. So if these people have been killed, I have problems to understand how you can come to 31 days. I don't know whether you would -- can answer or the witness can answer, to perhaps clarify this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is the document as we received it. I really don't know how it was written. What I do know is that when a soldier is killed, their families receive their salaries for the entire month and of course the witness may now correct me if I am wrong and I will ask the witness this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, am I correct when I think that if a soldier is killed, his family receives his salary for the entire month.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's play the video, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you hear -- somebody says, do we know who was killed here, the answer is a Serb. Slobodan Despotovic. Would you please now look at page 17 of this document. The name of Slobodan Despotovic, volunteer, who was killed in December 1992 is on this list, is it not? Could you please look.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Despotovic under number 44.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is his name on this list?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, witness. Now I would like the video to continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, those people that you saw, these are Serb soldiers, are they not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know them. Probably. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the insignia, the Kokarda insignia on the cap of -- not of this soldier but of the soldiers that you saw a little while ago?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these are Serb soldiers, are they not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at this man. This is Svetozar Andric, the commander of the Assault Brigade, is he not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you, witness, see the area, are you able to recognise the area?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this perhaps Voljevica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really tell on the basis of this video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you've seen this video. Were you able to recognise anyone in this video?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that this is actually the entrance to Voljevica, the village of Voljevica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at this man here. He is talking about the counterattack of Serbs in the direction of Bjelovac and Kunarac, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, Borivoje Tesic, is it not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, his name was mentioned, but I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me before the next question, just for purposes of the record, I understand that we must be submitting this or looking again at this defence exhibit for the images and not necessarily for the truth of what is being said on the video unless there will be testimony on that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think, Ms. Sellers, the same point was made on several occasions, both from your side and from the defence side, and I think the Trial Chamber has explained what their legal position is and the legal approach will be. So ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we don't need to worry about what we have raised. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we discussed that when D97 was admitted into evidence. Thank you very much, Your Honour. I would just like this large document that we discussed with the witness, I would like that to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that will be D256. Registrar, this has become D256.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the usher to show the witness two more documents. These are record files. You can perhaps take both of them together to save some time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at the record number 01321124. That deals with Zeljko Knezevic son of Vojislav. Please take a look at this document date and place of birth, the 30th of December. Or rather, -- rather -- no. Date and place of birth, the 30th of December, 1966, in Peteno Ilov [phoen], date and place when he was killed is the 16th of December, 1992. Kunjerac, killed in combat. Belonged to the Krajina Battalion. Witness, please look at this document and I will ask you something in relation to it. During your testimony yesterday, you claimed that on the 15th and the 16th of December, there was no combat in Bjelovac and around it. Kunjerac is the hill linked to Bjelovac. Therefore, does this document show something else?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain it to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated in my statement, as far as I can remember, that on the 15th there was no fire coming from the Muslim side when we were retrieving the bodies of the dead. If I remember, that's what I stated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 16th?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the 15th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the 16th?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was absent on the 16th. I attended a funeral and I don't know what happened. I just told you that there was no fire coming from the Muslim side on the previous day, because on that day we were collecting the dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do we agree that it states here, in this document, that this person was killed in combat on the 16th of December, 1992, in that area?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the document shows. However, I never heard of this person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So this is Zeljko Knezevic,, son of Vojislav?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know him and the village where he was born, I never heard about it before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. Petrovic, when giving evidence yesterday, you said that the Serb forces, as you called them, were issued an order to withdraw on the 17th of December, 1992, to withdraw from the Bjelovac area. I will ask you in relation to that, the following. At that time you were not a member of the command issuing this order?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not see the document related to this order?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also testified that you were not a member of the units carrying out combat activity on the 15th and 16th and 17th of December, but rather that you were in Bratunac or in Serbia, at that time. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, as for the fact that the order was issued, you don't have any valid information that could confirm it or disprove it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not. However, those who were in Bjelovac told me that it had been ordered that they withdraw from Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if they were misinformed, you were misinformed as well.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, please take a look at another record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, because I don't think it has been mentioned. The previous series of questions were related to the document, which is now going to be marked D257, and which bears ERN number 01321124.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, now please look at this second record, about the killing of a soldier. The soldier is Stanoje, Maric, son of Rade, born in of a soldier. The soldier is Stanoje, Maric, son of Rade, born 1952, in Strpci, killed on the 22nd of December 1992, in Voljevica, Pobrdje. Killed in combat. Was a member of the Krajina Battalion. Mr. Petrovic, do you agree with me that the Serb forces from this area did not withdraw on the 17th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree. This soldier who was killed was killed in Voljevica, in the area where the entry point in Voljevica is. The Serb troops were in Pobrdje at the time, whereas Muslims were in Voljevica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that they fought each other during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present. It is possible. However, this soldier and the document here do not pertain to Bjelovac. There was no one in Bjelovac at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like this document to be exhibited as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will be D258.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Something else in relation to this document that I wanted to ask you about. Therefore, in Bjelovac and in you about. Therefore, in Bjelovac and in its surrounding area, including Voljevica, Sikirici, Zaluzje, it wasn't only the second and the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade that were deployed together with the red berets but there was also the 6th Krajina Battalion. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will ask you some other questions now about the evidence you gave yesterday. You told us that the Muslims withdrew from Bjelovac at around 3.30 on the 14th of December, 1992. Actually, will you agree with me that simultaneously with their withdrawal or as they were withdrawing, they were subjected to a very intense shelling, launched from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that on the 14th of December, 1992, you were in Bjelovac the whole day. And you said that you noticed -- observed one plane bombing Bjelovac in the afternoon hours. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This plane dropped bombs on the houses in Bjelovac, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard two detonations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw one such crater in the vicinity of a house in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you can distinguish between the time of the day, you can distinguish between the morning and the afternoon, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I suggest to you that the bombing lasted much longer than you stated and that it actually started at 9.00 and 26 minutes in the morning; would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had to see this, or hear the sound of the planes, or the plane.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I both heard and saw the plane.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, witness. I will ask you something else now. The houses of the Jovanovic family are located in the vicinity of a large forest; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if this is a good time for a break, then I will ask for it, but I don't know. I might even be able to reduce my numbers -- my questions. Otherwise, if you think that we should continue, I can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's -- because I actually have my attention has been drawn by the registry to make sure, before the break, to know exactly where we stand. Because obviously if we spill over and need Monday, they have to make arrangements for interpreters and other things. Do you think you will finish your cross-examination today? And if you think you will, how much time do you think you still require?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I will definitely conclude the examination. Perhaps I need another 15 minutes, at the most. And this is why I wanted to consult my colleague, to see whether I can shorten this. But I will not require more than 15 minutes at any rate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On the assumption that you don't know what the rest of the questions and the rest of the answers are going to be during these 15 minutes, do you think there will be a re-examination on your part?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there will be a re-examination. It will be extremely brief, though. Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have any questions? We still have ten minutes for the break. Assuming that on past experience, 15 minutes by Madam Vidovic means 20 or 25, can we continue and then call it a day? Finish? From on the right I see nodding, on the left? Yes. Technicians? All right. So let's proceed and we won't have a break, we will continue until we finish, provided that we try to finish within the next 20, 25 minutes. We don't have any questions. I don't have any questions either. And there doesn't seem to be --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I just need one minute to consult my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I will ask you just several more questions now and will show you, I think, just one or perhaps two documents. The fighting around Bjelovac continued, in fact, until Bjelovac was once again taken by the Serbs. Do you have any knowledge of this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fighting did not continue until Bjelovac was taken again.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Could the usher please show a document to the witness. It has number, ERN number 00675457. This is a document of the Bratunac Brigade dated the 29th of January, 1993. Witness, please look at this document. This is a combat report sent to the command of the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, Drina Corps. I apologise for my mistake. I will now quote paragraph 6 to you. Can you find it? Please take a look at this. So, this is dated the 29th of January, 1992. Paragraph 6 says: Special Brigade and the 2nd Infantry Battalion, with artillery and tank support of the army of Yugoslavia, are to conduct activities in Voljevica, Kunjerac. The 2nd Battalion is the one we mentioned earlier. And I will ask you do you agree that the fighting for the second taking of Bjelovac, indeed took place? Does this document effect your position in any way?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I explain?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the attacks that were carried out from Bratunac towards Bjelovac. So the combat activities originated from Bratunac, as I've mentioned earlier. At the time there was no one in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please understand what I'm saying. I'm not trying to suggest to you or to prove to you that the fighting originated from Bjelovac. I'm simply asking you about combat activity in that area. I am not trying to prove that Bjelovac at that time was the epicentre of the world and that everything originated from there. Therefore, would you agree that when Bjelovac was retaken, there was a new combat waged there. Does this document affect your previous answer?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be exhibited, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will be exhibit -- yes, this will be exhibit, Defence Exhibit 259. Judge Eser?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I have a question with regard to the transcript in comparison to the document, the transcript reads --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please, for Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: In the transcript, we can read on line 23 of 71, paragraph 6 says: "Special Brigade of 2nd Infantry Battalion with artillery and with tank support of the army of Yugoslavia are to conduct activities in Voljevica, Kunjerac." Now at least in the English translation of the document, it is not mentioned that, the support of the Army of Yugoslavia. Just to make sure that we have a correct translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the document says as follows: "Tasks of the units, special brigades and the 2nd Infantry Battalion, together with artillery and tank support," and then in parenthesis it says: "VJ." Witness, do you agree that VJ stands for the army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the rest follows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: This was not contained in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. Thank you. In the future I will try to keep an eye on this. Could this document please be exhibited, if it hasn't been already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It has already become 259.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the usher to assist us and show another document to the witness. 01331837. This is the document of the command of the Light Infantry Brigade of Bratunac, the 2nd of February, 1993. Report sent to the command of the Drina Corps. Please take a look at this document, witness. I will show you just a very brief passage in that document. In paragraph 2, it says: Our forces are defending positions with artillery support, carrying out active operations on the axis, Zaluzje, Bjelovac. Do you know anything about these acts of operations conducted with artillery support in the direction of Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to that, I will ask you this. You, yourself, were not in Bjelovac after the Muslims entered the place and know nothing about what was going on there. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was there only on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. And you don't know whether there were civilians or soldiers in that area?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period following your departure from Bjelovac in January and February of 1993.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know nothing about it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can this document be also exhibited?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document will now become Defence Exhibit D260.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When testifying about Kemo who you have mentioned today, you said that before the war the police could do nothing to him. You will agree with me, won't you, that we in Bosnia-Herzegovina and in the former Yugoslavia had a very good and very well organised police force?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that police, as it was, could do nothing to Kemo, was completely helpless?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecutor showed a photograph to you, in which you recognised Mr. Oric. You have no idea who made that photograph or when?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, I have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. And I also wish to express my appreciation for having kept your cross-examination to an extent which would allow us to send the witness back home this weekend. Ms. Sellers, I understand you have a short - and I mean it - re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour very short. Re-examined by Ms. Sellers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you testified concerning the attack on Bjelovac during the cross-examination and the different houses that had burned. I just want to ask you. When you left Bjelovac, after the attack, and went to the funerals in Bratunac, did you speak to anyone or did anyone tell you at that time that fighting was continuing in Bjelovac on the 15th of December?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Bjelovac on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 16th. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The 15th they were collecting the bodies, the 16th he went to the funeral in Bratunac. So the question basically comes to this: On the 16th of December, when you were attending that funeral, during that day, did anyone tell you or bring to your attention that fighting was continuing in Bjelovac, on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 17th of December, you testified on cross-examination that you were in Serbia. And were you in Grabovica on the 17th, as you testified in direct examination?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was there in Grabovica on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now when you were in Grabovica on the 17th, and had occasion to look into Bjelovac, did you see any fighting or hear any fighting, exchanges of gunfire going on on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that the day that you saw the remaining part of the village burning, on the 17th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've been asked where your house was located on cross-examination and you've been asked about the other houses that burned in Bjelovac on cross-examination and I'm speaking about the 14th of December, 1992. When your house was burning, or the other houses, did you, at any time, hear the soldiers ask people to come out of their houses prior to them being burned?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also in cross-examination you said that you -- you testified that you did not have any weapons on the 14th and that you spent that day at your sister's house. Therefore, would it be true to state that when your house burned on the 14th, that there was no gunfire coming from your house, there was no one in your house that was defending your house or causing your house at that moment to be a military target?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that question was specifically put to him and answered during cross.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I think he has made it clear there was no one with a weapon inside the house and there was no shooting from the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has answered that question already.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So I can take that as being confirmed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he has answered the question. If you doubt my word, and it won't be the first time I have made a mistake, we can check the transcript. But he said -- I'm quite positive about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Then that's the extent of my re-exam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because he explained how his weapon was in the trench, how his brother who is slightly retarded never handled a weapon, and how the other person, his cousin or nephew, or whatever, did not have a weapon. The weapon was in the trench in front of the house, he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm confirming in his house, not in his sister's house, there was no gunfire coming out of that house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No further questions? I don't have any further questions either. We made it, Mr. Petrovic. I was afraid that you would have had to stay here the weekend and then Monday and then possibly leave Tuesday or Wednesday, but you will be able to go back to your family this weekend. I am sure that our Staff will have already started making all of the necessary arrangements to return you back home. On behalf of Judge Brydensholt, Judge Eser, and myself, and on behalf of the Tribunal, I wish to thank you for having come over to give testimony. And on behalf of everyone, I also wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, you may escort the witness out. Let's conclude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Monday, therefore, we are not sitting. Tuesday we will have that meeting. You will -- I think I was told the time but I've forgotten it. I haven't forgotten it. I jotted it down but I know it's in the afternoon. But there was a question on -- because of who will be attending and I think it could be shifted to 2.30. I don't know. But anyway, 2.30, I think. 3.00? 3.00, yes. All right. So that's it. By today you are supposed to make available the statements of the witnesses you want to produce, additional witnesses, so that masochistically we would have spent the weekend going through them to see where we stand, but it seems that you don't want us to work over the weekend, Mr. Wubben. Have you received that already?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It should be, and in addition, I can confirm that the witness that was projected to be interviewed for the pending days is still at that process. So you can't have received that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, but that is understandable. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: There is, however, one I need to check. Pleas bear me a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before -- while Mr. Wubben is checking, I think it is my responsibility to thank, once more, the staff, the interpreters, the technicians, and the courtroom staff for having cooperated. I know that sitting for almost two hours at a stretch is tiring. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I've been confirmed that, indeed, we -- apart from that witness, we have distributed and there was also this witness who has already testified but will be very limited extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That statement should also -- and it might be one page or two pages, I don't know, should also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. Have a nice weekend, all of you, and see you again on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
